A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RollingDepth in Video Depth without Video Models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplements are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation experiments on PointOdyssey, ScanNet, Bonn and DyDToF, component ablations, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original temporal-smoothness, DDAD, and inference-efficiency results in Tables S1–S4.

M1.justification: The snippet-based inverse-depth model, cross-frame attention, dilated sampling, co-alignment and optional refinement remain unchanged. The added statement about latent-space MSE clarifies existing training rather than establishing a changed objective.

E1.justification: Section B.2 adds evaluation on DDAD driving scenes with sparse depth annotations, a focused extension of domain coverage. Existing training datasets, four main evaluation datasets and the video-depth task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same six baselines. Table S4 adds NVDS to the runtime comparison, which v1 reported only against ChronoDepth and DepthCrafter. The new DDAD and smoothness comparisons otherwise use previously evaluated methods.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation with GMFlow-based OPW measurements, failure-excluded subsets, 100-frame DDAD sequences and a larger-batch efficiency setting. Section 4.2 also changes the stated ScanNet procedure to select 270 frames before threefold downsampling, matching the existing 90-frame table header. Unchanged main scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table S2 extends the existing dilation ablation with OPW measurements, testing the relationship between geometric accuracy and local smoothness. Table S1 additionally examines sensitivity to catastrophic baseline failures through filtered-subset results. Existing component ablations and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Section B.3 newly specifies ten inference repetitions after a warm-up iteration and reports mean runtime. v1's timing discussion gives no repetition count. This is additional reporting, not evidence that an earlier run count increased; no confidence intervals or variability estimates are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values, while Tables S1–S4 add substantial smoothness, DDAD and efficiency results. DDAD reports RollingDepth at 12.8% AbsRel and 83.2% delta1 versus DepthCrafter's 19.3% and 74.8%. S1 also shows DepthCrafter ahead on failure-excluded PointOdyssey OPW, despite RollingDepth's better full-set result.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective and co-alignment mathematics, including Equations 1–5, are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation accompanies the additional evaluations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about accurate, temporally consistent video depth from an image diffusion model. The new experiments support existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section B.1 newly explains that OPW measures adjacent-frame smoothness rather than long-term consistency or geometric accuracy. It hypothesizes that larger dilation improves geometry at some cost to local smoothness. Existing explanations of video-model failures and RollingDepth's cloudy-sky and glass limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 explicitly documents latent-space MSE training. B.3 adds RTX3090 hardware, warm-up and model-residency information, while Table S4 explains increased inference batching. These improve implementation and benchmarking documentation; existing training hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references, including DDAD's source, GMFlow, UniDepthV2 and FutureDepth. These provide additional methodological and related-work context without substantially changing the paper's positioning against video-diffusion approaches.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language edits, removes redundant wording in Section 3.3, and corrects Appendix A.1's reference from Section 3.5 to 3.3. The appendix becomes Supplementary Material, with three new subsections preceding the renumbered failure discussions; the main narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Four supplementary tables are added; S2 redisplays Table 2's accuracy results with new OPW columns. Main figures and tables retain their displays. Existing failure Figures S2–S3 move to the final page with altered spacing, producing a localized supplement-layout expansion.

improvement.justification: New smoothness measurements and the explicit warning that OPW misses long-term consistency improve support and qualification of the temporal-coherence claim. DDAD and timing/memory results add useful validation beyond v1. The improvement is limited by unspecified failure-exclusion lists and inference batch sizes, plus Table S2's ambiguous scaling caption.
